html:
Spanish writer, born in 1547 near Madrid, who wrote Don Quixote, often called the first modern novel and the greatest work in the Spanish language.

His own life was an adventure. As a young soldier he fought at the Battle of Lepanto in 1571, where a wound left his left hand useless. On the way home in 1575 his ship was taken by Barbary corsairs, and he spent five years as a captive in Algiers. He tried to escape four times before he was ransomed.

Back in Spain he worked as a tax collector and buyer of supplies for the navy, and went to prison more than once over his accounts. Fame came late. The first part of Don Quixote appeared in 1605, when he was in his fifties, and the second in 1615. He also wrote plays and short stories, the Exemplary Novels.

He died in Madrid in April 1616, days apart from William Shakespeare. Spanish is sometimes called "the language of Cervantes", and he is the central figure of the Spanish Golden Age of letters.
sum: Spanish writer, born in 1547 near Madrid, who wrote Don Quixote, often called the first modern novel and the greatest work in the Spanish language.
